about.title: Morgan Hill Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Morgan Hill's mix of agriculture, warehousing, construction and light industry along corridors like Monterey Road and Butterfield Boulevard means workplace injuries here often involve heavy equipment, vehicles, or third-party contractors moving through busy job sites. When you're hurt at work, California law generally routes your claim through workers' compensation regardless of fault — but that's not always the whole story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to the accident, you may also have a separate claim outside the workers' comp system. Santa Clara County work sites, from warehouses near US-101 to smaller commercial lots off Dunne Avenue, see their share of forklift accidents, falls, and vehicle-related injuries. Sorting out whether a third party is involved takes a careful look at how the injury happened. LawProactive connects injured workers in Morgan Hill with an independent attorney, free of charge, who can review the details and explain what options might apply to your situation.

Injuries from defective tools or machinery

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Morgan Hill Work Injury

items.title: Understanding the 30-Day Reporting Window
items.desc: California requires injured workers to report the incident to their employer within 30 days to preserve workers' comp benefits. An attorney can help make sure this step doesn't get missed or mishandled.

items.title: Spotting a Third-Party Claim
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, equipment maker, or other driver on the job site may open the door to a separate claim. An independent attorney can evaluate whether that applies to your accident.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law prohibits employer retaliation against workers who report injuries or file claims. If you're worried about your job while recovering, an attorney can explain your rights and the deadlines that protect them, including the 2-year window for third-party claims.

items.question: I was hurt at a warehouse near US-101 in Morgan Hill — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is your primary path against your employer, regardless of who was at fault. However, if a third party — like a delivery driver, contractor, or equipment supplier — contributed to your injury, you may also have a separate claim against them. An independent attorney can look at the specifics and let you know which paths apply.

items.question: What if my employer says my injury doesn't qualify because I didn't report it right away?
items.answer: California generally requires injuries be reported within 30 days, so timing matters. That said, missing the exact date doesn't automatically end your options — an attorney can review what happened and advise on next steps.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a workers' comp claim in Morgan Hill?
items.answer: No — California law prohibits retaliation against employees for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an independent attorney can explain what protections and remedies may be available to you.
